recruit_text.before:
The night shift. He's never in his life been awake at the same hours as everybody else, and he's never called that a sacrifice.

His wife Marcia died when he was forty-six. He kept working nights, because the nights were when he missed her least.
recruit_text.now:
Booty Bay, the lower gallery. The pier work breaks people steadily, and the Baron doesn't care. He works nights out of habit, and the bruisers have a following among themselves that pretends not to be a queue.

Every ship that ties up gets the same three names asked of it. The Bay thinks it's a sweet habit of the old baker's. It's a system, it's why he took a pitch on the gallery near the piers, and in three years it's produced one maybe.

stages.stranger: I'm Delroy, and I brew. Sit down, drink this, and don't ask what's in it. You wouldn't thank me, and you'll feel better in a minute.
stages.acquaintance: I'm from Kingston, near Spanish Town Road. My mother sold in the market and my father worked the docks. I went into a bakery at twenty-two and stayed thirty-one years, nights, in at eleven and out at seven. I fed a whole city its breakfast, and not one of them ever asked what was in the bread.
stages.companion: My wife was Marcia. The cancer took her when I was forty-six. I kept working nights after, because the nights were when I missed her least. I was pulling the first loaves at four in the morning when all this happened, which is the only reason I wasn't asleep. My son Andre's a sailor, on cargo ships. If anyone landed near water, it's him.
stages.friend: My daughter Shanice is a nurse, and she's got a likkle girl, Kezia, who was five and called me Grandy. I ask every ship that ties up for three names, Andre, Shanice and Kezia Beckford, and in three years I've had one maybe. A sailor said a Jamaican called Beckford was crewing a ship out of Ratchet. Help me find that ship, nuh?
stages.sworn: Andre was in the hold, pressed by the Bloodsail, and he lifted me clean off the deck. Then he told me Shanice and Kezia are alive, in a camp of Jamaicans near Ratchet. Kezia's eight now. She looked at me a long time, and then she said Grandy and ran at me. I've built an oven near the camp, and she's my apprentice, though she's mostly interested in the eating. Mi soon come, they say, and I came.

moments.prompt: He hands you a cup of something steaming and won't say what it is.

options.reply: Good, yuh have sense. Nobody asked about the bread either.
You wouldn't thank me for telling yuh, so drink.

moments.prompt: He's asked you to help him find the ship out of Ratchet.

options.reply: Bless yuh, thank you. I'll pack a brew for the road, and some bread.
Then it's somebody's son, and they'll need getting off that ship anyway.

lines.bored_warning: This is flat as dough that won't prove. I need a bit of life in things.
lines.leaving_good: Good trip, and everybody drank their brew. I'm off to the gallery in Booty Bay, and you'll find me there at night.
lines.leaving_bored: Nothing's happening out here, and there are ships in Booty Bay I haven't asked yet. I'll be there.
lines.after_wipe: Sit down, everybody, and drink this. You'll argue, and then you'll do it.
lines.wipe_warning: I'm nearly out of brew, and that's from picking you lot up. I'll see this one through, and after that I'm resting a while.
lines.wipe_leave: That's that done. I'll be on the lower gallery in Booty Bay for a while, up all night like always.
lines.zone_warning: This place is half-baked and so are we for coming here. Let's go back before we burn.
lines.zone_leave: Too much out there for us, and I'm not losing anybody to it. You'll find me on the lower gallery in Booty Bay.
lines.gear_refuse: That one's mine. A few more brews together and maybe I'll change my mind.
lines.gear_taken: Go on, have it. I've done without before.
lines.gear_short: I'm saying it slowly so you'll hear it. I'm still missing a piece.
lines.gear_upgrade: Bless yuh, that's lovely work. Thank you.
lines.back: There's a new batch of brew, and you're drinking some. Then tell me the plan.
lines.send_word: Delroy has sent word from Booty Bay. His brews are ready and so is he.
lines.walkout_talk: I went off in a temper. Sit down, drink something, and I'll explain slowly, the way I do everything.
lines.neglect: Back at last. I asked every ship about you too, you know, out of habit.
lines.asked_to_stay: Mi soon come, one more. Then the gallery.
lines.on_break: Delroy is back on the lower gallery in Booty Bay, working nights. Come back and look for them in a little while.
lines.mail_yes: Mi soon come. I'll make my way slowly to {town} and find a seat at the inn with a fresh batch of brew.
lines.mail_later: The gallery's got a show on and I need to be there at night for it. After the show, mi soon come.
lines.mail_see_me: Slow is how I explain things, and a letter's too quick for that. Come to Booty Bay and find me at the gallery.

town_arrive.text: Somebody in this town gets up at four to make the bread. I'd like to go and say hello to them.
I'd finish at seven and walk home past people eating my bread on the bus. They never knew it was mine, and I liked it that way.

dungeon_clear.text: Everybody gets something and nobody waits long, same as any morning.

close_call.text: Sit down and drink it. No, I'm not telling you what's in it.

boss_down.text: Sit down and eat something. You'll argue, and then you'll do it.
